data: © NASA/JPL-Caltech — Jezero Crater landing site; carries the Ingenuity helicopter (88 flights, retired Jan 2024).

Designed to cache promising rock cores for a future Mars Sample Return mission. Already drilled and sealed 26+ samples by mid-2024. The Ingenuity helicopter — originally a 30-day technology demo — flew 72 times before damaging a rotor in January 2024. First powered, controlled flight on another world.
First Mars sample-caching for future return; first powered flight in another atmosphere (Ingenuity).

Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021 — a 3.8-billion-year-old river delta selected because it held the best chance of preserving evidence of ancient Martian life. The rover carries the first Mars helicopter (Ingenuity), the first Mars audio recorder, and the first sample-caching system. Sample tubes left on the surface will be returned to Earth by the Mars Sample Return mission in the 2030s.
Perseverance during assembly at JPL — 1025 kg, MMRTG-powered, carrying 23 cameras, 2 microphones, and a sample-caching turret.
The Ingenuity helicopter mounted to Perseverance's belly — the first heavier-than-air vehicle to fly on another planet.
July 30, 2020 — Atlas V from Cape Canaveral
Atlas V 541 launches Mars 2020 from SLC-41, July 30 2020 07:50 EDT — 203-day transit to Jezero.
Van Zyl Overlook — Mastcam-Z first 360° panorama, sol 3 (Feb 21, 2021). The Jezero delta is visible to the west.
Perseverance + its traverse, photographed from orbit by Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter's HiRISE camera at 25 cm/pixel.
First Ingenuity flight, April 19 2021 — a 3-second hover at 3 m altitude. The Wright Brothers' Flyer carried a swatch of fabric on the helicopter for this exact moment.
First sample tube sealed and cached on the Martian surface — "Roubion" core, drilled from Rochette boulder, September 2021.
Organic molecules detected in the Wildcat Ridge mudstone by the SHERLOC instrument — a chemical fingerprint of ancient Martian biology candidates.
Orrery reference map of CTX imagery and the Perseverance traverse data

Illustrated block map of Perseverance’s route across Jezero Crater since 2021: from the landing site (sol 0) past Ingenuity’s Flight 1 (sol 58), the first core (sol 190), Hawksbill Gap (sol 440), Three Forks Depot (sol 653) and the Margin unit (sol 915) to the rover’s position on sol 2022.
First helicopter on another planet (Ingenuity); first sample caching on Mars
